I hit the tool limit mid-build. Here's where things stand — the analysis is complete and the first files are written, but the archive is not finished, so please don't apply anything yet. Let me give you the findings so the next session can resume cleanly.

What I found (M6 Slice 24 — response security headers)
Starting point verified from dump.txt: Slice 23 landed, 1005 tests, 15/15 E2E green, docs/_append/ retired.

I reviewed a layer nothing in the tree had ever looked at, and there are two real findings.

F-49a — the application publishes no security headers, and it has a Content-Security-Policy it never wrote. There is not one mention of CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or frame-ancestors anywhere in the tree — not in the app, not in Caddyfile, not in any document. But AddInteractiveServerRenderMode() installs an endpoint convention (verified against dotnet/aspnetcore release/10.0, ServerRazorComponentsEndpointConventionBuilderExtensions.cs) that appends frame-ancestors 'self' to Content-Security-Policy — the framework's mitigation for WebSocket-compression-plus-framing. So the app has carried a one-directive CSP since M1, on component endpoints only (not static files, not /healthz/*, not the clock, not the sign-out POST), and it appends with StringValues.Concat, so a hand-written policy would arrive beside it, not instead of it.

F-49b — connect-src 'self' would have killed every circuit in the E2E harness. CSP3's 'self' is an origin comparison; the spec's own "Changes from Level 2" only extends it to https: and wss:. ws: from an http: page is exactly what a bare dotnet run and the §16.3 harness serve, and MDN still carries the interop warning. The policy therefore names ws://{host} wss://{host} derived from the request's own (already PublicOriginMiddleware-normalised) host.

Supporting facts I computed rather than assumed: zero inline <script>, zero inline event handlers, zero url(/@import in app.css, zero external origins anywhere; 21 components carry <style> blocks (2,388 lines) and Blazor's reconnect overlay builds one at runtime via innerHTML, so style-src 'unsafe-inline' is earned, not lazy; the data:, favicon is the only data: URL, and <link rel=icon> is an img-src fetch.

M6 Slice 24 — F-49. 13 full files, extracts at the repo root. Nothing to delete.

bash
tar -xzf m6-slice-24-response-security-headers.tar.gz -C /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
cd /home/kushal/src/dotnet/myrestaurant
git add src/MyRestaurant.WebApplication/Security \
        tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Security \
        docs/adr/0013-security-headers-are-the-applications.md
There is a Program.cs edit — two changes. Flagging it because they're rare.

The finding
Searching for Content-Security-Policy in the tree returns nothing. That isn't the finding.

AddInteractiveServerRenderMode() — the parameterless call, unchanged since M1 — installs an endpoint convention that appends frame-ancestors 'self'. Read out of dotnet/aspnetcore at release/10.0, its enabling condition holds on both of your defaults. Every page you have ever served carried a Content Security Policy. One directive, at 'self', on component endpoints only — not app.css, not js/*.js, not /_framework/*, not /healthz/*, not the clock, not the sign-out POST, not a 404 or a 429. And it appends with StringValues.Concat, so anything written beside it would have been delivered beside it.

A control that existed, worked, and was never decided on. That's a shape your ledger had no row for.

The second half is why this is a slice. connect-src 'self' — the obvious choice — would have passed every unit test and refused the circuit's WebSocket on every plain-HTTP origin, because 'self' is an origin comparison and CSP3's carve-out covers wss: but not ws:. That's dotnet run and all fifteen E2E scenarios. So connect-src names ws://{host} wss://{host} from the request. What would have caught the mistake is Slice 23's work: a policy that kills the circuit is one where nothing reports data-live='true'.

Expected
dotnet test → 1051, 0 failed (was 1005; 29 + 8 + 9)
MYRESTAURANT_E2E=1 → 15 passed, 0 skipped — the one that matters, real Chromium enforcing a real CSP over plain http
check_tree.sh authored-text count +6
All 46 assertions were executed here as faithful ports and pass; sensitivity proven by planting an inline <script>, an inline onclick, a CDN script and a second data: URL. SpecificationVersionTests re-verified against the edited spec (1.9, descending). BUILD_PROGRESS.md confirmed byte-identical prefix plus one appended section.
